title: Use and connect mathematical representations
subtitle: Help students see one idea in many forms — and, above all, the links between them. The connections are where understanding lives.

sections.sources: Source: NCTM, Principles to Actions (2014) · Lesh Translation Model · Adding It Up (2001).

blocks.text: Effective teaching engages students in making connections among mathematical representations to deepen understanding and to use them as tools for solving problems.

NCTM names five kinds of representation — **contextual, visual, verbal, physical, and symbolic**. Understanding grows less from any single one than from the *arrows between them*: seeing that this graph, this table, this equation, and this story are all the same relationship. In 6–8 this is the spine of the ratios → proportional-relationships → linear-functions progression.
What it looks like in grades 6–8

items: A relationship shown as a table, a graph, an equation, and a context — side by side.
The teacher asking “where is the slope in the table? in the graph? in the equation?”
Students moving between forms on purpose, choosing the one that helps them solve.
Concrete and visual models used to make abstract symbols meaningful, not as decoration.

yes.title: We want to see & hear
items: Explicit links: “This 3 in the equation — where is it on the graph?”
Students picking a representation to solve a problem
Diagrams and tables treated as thinking tools

no.title: We should *not* see
items: Representations shown but never connected to each other
A graph drawn once and abandoned
Manipulatives as a reward, disconnected from the math

blocks.text: Where it lives in our toolbelt

This practice *is* [Connecting Representations](/math/approach/connecting-representations). It also powers [Quick Images](/math/approach/quick-images), the visual arguments in [Same But Different / WODB](/math/approach/same-but-different), and the “connect” phase of the [5 Practices](/math/approach/five-practices).
When a student gives an answer in one form, ask the class to produce it in another — then ask where the same number lives in both. The naming of that link is the learning.
